title: Boundary rectifiability in ℝ^P for compactly supported integer multiplicity currents of finite mass and boundary mass, from (DTr) and CL_P(d) (Simon Ch. 6, 6.2 first case and 6.3; supplied steps 5–6)
statement: Assume (DTr), the in-range deformation theorem, verbatim the corresponding hypothesis of the parent (the first conjunct of the sibling deformation, dtc_bc_tc_cl_deformation_isoperimetric): for P, m ∈ ℕ with m + 1 < P there is c ∈ ℝ≥0, c ≥ 1, such that for every ρ > 0 and every integer multiplicity T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with compact support, M(T) < ∞ and M(∂T) < ∞ there are Q, S ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) and R ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) with Q, ∂Q, R integer multiplicity, T − Q − S = ∂R, Q = 0 or M(Q) ≥ ρ^{m+1}, M(Q) ≤ cM(T), M(∂Q) ≤ cM(∂T), M(R) ≤ cρM(T), M(S) ≤ cρM(∂T), spt Q ∪ spt R ⊆ thickening(3√Pρ, spt T) and spt ∂Q ∪ spt S ⊆ thickening(3√Pρ, spt ∂T). Let P, d ∈ ℕ with d + 1 < P and assume CL_P(d), verbatim the parent's hypothesis: for every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and T_j, T ∈ 𝒟_d(U), if every T_j is integer multiplicity, sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U (boundaryMassOn(T_j, W) = M_W(∂T_j), read as 0 in degree 0) and T_j ⇀ T, then T is integer multiplicity. Then every integer multiplicity T ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with compact support, M(T) < ∞ and M(∂T) < ∞ has integer multiplicity boundary ∂T. Notation: SimonGMT currents on the domain univ = ℝ^P, M = mass, M_W = massOn W, spt = support, ⇀ = WeaklyConvergesOn, IM = IsIntegerMultiplicity.
